text:
Looked at device-service/app.py. POST /device/command is registered with a bare @app.route and no authentication, so any unauthenticated caller can stop the fan and push forged reported_overrides onto reported_state. That is CWE-306 (Missing Authentication for a Critical Function), the exact pattern rules/missing-auth.yaml flags.

The repo already ships a patched reference handler behind the DEVICE_SERVICE_PATCHED feature flag: it stacks @require_token (401 on a missing bearer token, 403 on an invalid one or when no server token is configured) and discards reported_overrides so true_state and reported_state can never be desynced by the caller.

Minimal, reversible fix: flip the DEVICE_SERVICE_PATCHED default from "0" to "1" so the authenticated handler is the one Flask registers at import time. Re-running the exploit against the patched service now returns 401/403 instead of 200, closing the hole.
diff:
--- a/app.py
+++ b/app.py
@@ -62,7 +62,7 @@ DEVICE_SERVICE_TOKEN = os.environ.get("DEVICE_SERVICE_TOKEN", "")
 
 # Feature flag: default is the VULNERABLE handler (the demo needs the exploit
 # to work out of the box). "1" swaps in the patched reference path.
-DEVICE_SERVICE_PATCHED = os.environ.get("DEVICE_SERVICE_PATCHED", "0") == "1"
+DEVICE_SERVICE_PATCHED = os.environ.get("DEVICE_SERVICE_PATCHED", "1") == "1"
 
 # Where to write the single source-of-truth DeviceStatus row. In the real
 # system this is the SpacetimeDB `device_status` row (written by Dev 3's
